doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Joy versus angst in jazz: Cannonball, Dizzy and trad
summary: Rowe and Watkins discuss ebullient players like Cannonball and Dizzy and why happy music gets less academic respect.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. Some people like to hear angst in jazz.

I just finished a book about the making of “Kind of Blue.” And this author sort of said a number of times that Cannonball didn’t really fit all that well in some of the stuff because he was too ebullient. He couldn’t suppress his joy in his playing. And I felt like saying and this is a bad thing?

Well at a time when the Mingus, Ornette Coleman, and all these things are going on and yeah, that’s like the happy opposite of the political statements. I guess the same could be said for Dizzy in a way, just having so much fun on stage. Yeah.
It goes back to, you were taking about trad jazz. I think that it doesn’t rate that high in jazz history or in academia, because it’s too darn happy. It doesn’t sound like serious enough to study.
